title: Rust: String Basics
description: Work with string literals and the String type in Rust.

steps.title: String Literal (&str)
steps.description: Declare a string literal `greeting: &str = "Hello, Rust!"` and print it.

verification.failureMessage: Declare a &str variable and print it.

steps.title: String Type
steps.description: Create a `String` from a string literal using `to_string()` and print it.

verification.failureMessage: Create a String using to_string() and print it.

steps.title: String Concatenation
steps.description: Concatenate three strings: `"Rust"`, `" is "`, `"awesome"` using `+` or `format!`. Print the result.
hints: `format!` is usually cleaner for combining multiple strings.

verification.failureMessage: Combine 'Rust', 'is', and 'awesome' into one string and print it.

steps.title: String Length
steps.description: Declare a string `text = "Hello, 世界"` and print its length using `.len()`.
hints: `text.len()` returns the number of bytes, not characters.
Print both byte length and character count.

verification.failureMessage: Print the byte length of 'Hello, 世界'.

steps.title: String Interpolation
steps.description: Use `format!` to create a string like `"My name is X and I am Y years old"` with variables `name` and `age`. Print it.
hints: `let info = format!("My name is {} and I am {} years old", name, age);`
`format!` works like `println!` but returns a String instead of printing.

verification.failureMessage: Use format! to create and print a formatted string.
